title: Coronation Chicken
subtitle: Cold chicken in curried mayonnaise with apricot
excerpt: Poached chicken thighs coated in a sauce of mayonnaise, curry powder, and apricot, served cold. Created for the coronation banquet of Queen Elizabeth II in 1953 and still a British picnic and sandwich staple.

recipe.sourceNotes: Coronation chicken was created by Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume for the coronation banquet of Queen Elizabeth II on 2 June 1953, when it was served to 350 dignitaries. The original recipe used a French dressing base; the more common modern version uses mayonnaise. The dish was designed to be made ahead and served cold at a large gathering. It has become one of the most widely recognised post-war British dishes.

content.text: The sauce should be mildly spiced and sweet, not particularly hot. The curry powder should be a mild variety; Madras powder will make the sauce far too fiery for its intended purpose. Poach the chicken rather than roasting it so it stays moist enough to bind with the sauce. The sauce itself can be made 2 days ahead; dress the chicken no more than a few hours before serving.

Poach the chicken: put the thighs in a pan, cover with cold water, add the bay leaves and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer, skim, and cook for 20 minutes until cooked through. Remove, cool, and cut into bite-sized chunks.

Make the sauce: fry the onion in the oil over low heat for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garam masala and turmeric and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 more minute. Remove from the heat and cool completely.
Combine the cooled spice mixture with the mayonnaise, yoghurt, apricot jam, and lemon juice. Stir until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Taste: it should be mild, slightly sweet, and aromatic.
Fold the chicken pieces through the sauce. Refrigerate until needed. Serve on lettuce leaves or in sandwiches, scattered with fresh coriander.
